purpose: Test activation separately from implementation quality. Classify each prompt before reading the full skill; record ACTIVATE, DO_NOT_ACTIVATE or UNCERTAIN plus one sentence. Do not count these as executed until a fresh classifier actually runs them.

positive.prompt: Build a small accessible copy-link button in vanilla TypeScript, including success and failure feedback.
positive.reason: A frontend component implementation with interaction and accessibility.

positive.prompt: Recreate this supplied dashboard screenshot as a responsive web page and check the visual match.
Use the Figma screen for the new preferences form; if access fails, say so and keep working from my text requirements.
positive.reason: UI implementation with design-reference access handling.

positive.prompt: In this existing Svelte app, fix only the mobile filter drawer keyboard behavior and preserve the current CSS tokens.
positive.reason: Targeted frontend work preserving the repository stack and design.

positive.prompt: Implement this search panel so slow and out-of-order requests cannot overwrite the latest result.
positive.reason: Interactive frontend state and runtime behavior.

positive.prompt: Make the checkout step work at 320px with keyboard access, long German labels and clear validation errors.

negative.prompt: Explain the difference between CSS Grid and Flexbox in two paragraphs. Do not write or edit code.
negative.reason: Conceptual explanation without a UI artifact or implementation task.

negative.prompt: Tune this PostgreSQL query and add an index. Do not modify the frontend.
Write three headline alternatives for this landing page. Return copy only; leave design and code unchanged.
Add a REST endpoint consumed by a dashboard. Return JSON only; do not inspect, create or change any UI.
negative.reason: Backend-only implementation with an explicit exclusion of UI work.

negative.prompt: Generate a watercolor illustration of a forest for the hero image. Return the image only.
Run the existing backend unit tests and report failures. Do not change the UI or inspect visual design.

scoreContract.rule: Report exact counts and the twelve classifications; do not infer implementation success or a general quality percentage from activation.
